<h1 id="alerter-system-api">Alerter System API v1.6.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

<p>This is the <a href="/">Alerter System</a> API playground. More documentation is available at the <a href="/help/developers/">API Help Center</a>.</p><p>The "Available Authorizations" in the Authorize popup only applies to this playground web interface. Other <a href="/help/developers/authorization/">authorizations</a> are available for the actual API.</p>

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://api.apis.guru/">https://api.apis.guru/</a>

# Authentication

- oAuth2 authentication. OAuth 2.0 client credentials Grant

    - Flow: clientCredentials
    - Token URL = [/oauth/v2/access-token/](/oauth/v2/access-token/)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|full|Full access|
|read|Read-only access|

<h1 id="alerter-system-api-alertlog">AlertLog</h1>

## Retrieves the collection of AlertLog resources.

<a id="opIdapi_alert-log_get_collection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/alert-log \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/alert-log`

Retrieves the collection of AlertLog resources.

<h3 id="retrieves-the-collection-of-alertlog-resources-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer|false|The collection page number|
|dataSegmentCode|query|string|false|none|
|dataSegmentCode[]|query|[string]|false|none|
|monitor|query|string|false|none|
|monitor[]|query|[string]|false|none|
|alertService|query|string|false|none|
|alertService[]|query|[string]|false|none|
|alertLogStatusCode|query|string|false|none|
|alertLogStatusCode[]|query|[string]|false|none|
|partition|query|string|false|none|
|partition[]|query|[string]|false|none|
|properties[]|query|[string]|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "alertLogErrorMessage": "string",
    "alertLogMessageId": "string",
    "alertLogStatusCode": "string",
    "alertService": "string",
    "createdAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "dataSegmentCode": "string",
    "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "monitor": "string",
    "partition": "string",
    "ping": "string",
    "resourceOwner": "string",
    "webhookResponseBody": "string",
    "webhookResponseHeaders": [
      "string"
    ]
  }
]
```

<h3 id="retrieves-the-collection-of-alertlog-resources-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|AlertLog collection|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests|None|

<h3 id="retrieves-the-collection-of-alertlog-resources-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[AlertLog-get](#schemaalertlog-get)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth
</aside>

<h3 id="creates-a-alertservice-resource-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AlertService-post](#schemaalertservice-post)|true|The new AlertService resource|
|» alertServiceName|body|string \| null|true|The name of the alert service. Max 255 characters.|
|» alertServiceNotes|body|string \| null|false|Notes about the alert service. Max 10,000 characters. Formatting using Markdown is allowed. HTML will be removed.|
|» alertServiceTransportCode|body|string(iri-reference) \| null|true|The transport of the alert service.|
|» dataSegmentCode|body|string \| null|false|User-provided string on which to segment and filter data. Max 50 characters.|
|» mediaObjects|body|[string(iri-reference)]|false|Media objects that must be sent with each alert. Only applicable when you use your own email alert services.|
|» partition|body|string(iri-reference)|true|The partition that contains this resource instance. The resource cannot be moved to another partition.|
|» recipientEmailAddress|body|string(email) \| null|true|The email address where alerts will be sent.|
|» recipientPhoneNumber|body|string \| null|true|The phone number where alerts will be sent. Ensure that the number format complies with the external transport service that will send the alert.|

`POST /api/monitor`

Creates a Monitor resource.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "alertPayloadExtended": "string",
  "alertPayloadShort": "string",
  "alertServices": [
    "string"
  ],
  "allowUnauthenticatedPings": true,
  "contentCheckMustNotExist": true,
  "contentCheckText": "string",
  "contentCheckUrl": "http://example.com",
  "contentCheckXpathFilter": "string",
  "dataSegmentCode": "string",
  "graceSeconds": 0,
  "intervalDays": 0,
  "intervalHours": 0,
  "intervalMinutes": 0,
  "intervalMonths": 0,
  "intervalSeconds": 0,
  "intervalYears": 0,
  "isMonitorPaused": true,
  "monitorName": "string",
  "monitorNotes": "string",
  "monitorTypeCode": "string",
  "partition": "string",
  "publicDescription": "string",
  "startMonitorAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "timezoneCode": "string",
  "webResponseSecondsLimit": 0,
  "webResponseUrl": "http://example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="creates-a-monitor-resource-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[Monitor-post](#schemamonitor-post)|true|The new Monitor resource|
|» alertPayloadExtended|body|string \| null|false|Payload that must be sent in the body of each alert when you use your own email or webhook alert services. This is the body for email alerts and the request body for webhook alerts. This text is not sent when using the built-in alert services. Sending user-supplied text via our own email server is too big a risk to our email reputation. Max 2 MB characters.|
|» alertPayloadShort|body|string \| null|false|Payload that must be sent in the body of each alert when you use your own short message alert services. This also serves as the subject for email alerts. Not used for webhooks. This text is not sent when using the built-in alert services. Sending user-supplied text via our own email server is too big a risk to our email reputation. Max 100 characters.|
|» alertServices|body|[string(iri-reference)]|false|The alert services that are related to this resource.|
|» allowUnauthenticatedPings|body|boolean|false|Indicates that the monitor will accept pings that are not OAuth authenticated.|
|» contentCheckMustNotExist|body|boolean|false|Indicates that the Web Content monitor must verify the absence of the text or the Xpath node, and dispatch an alert if it is present. The default behavior is to verify the presence of the text or the Xpath node, and dispatch an alert if it is absent.|
|» contentCheckText|body|string \| null|false|The text (case-insensitive) that must or must not be present at the contentCheckUrl. If contentCheckXpathFilter is supplied, then the only the text within that nodes is evaluated, otherwise text on the entire web page is evaluated.|
|» contentCheckUrl|body|string(uri) \| null|false|The URL that the Web Content monitor type must evaluate for the specified conditions.|
|» contentCheckXpathFilter|body|string \| null|false|The Xpath filter (<a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XPath">Xpath</a>, <a href="https://devhints.io/xpath">Xpath Cheatsheet</a>) that selects a specific node in the HTML of the target web page. If contentCheckText is supplied, then only the text within the selected node is evaluated. If contentCheckText is left empty, then the presence or the absence of the selected node is evaluated.|
|» dataSegmentCode|body|string \| null|false|User-provided string on which to segment and filter data. Max 50 characters.|
|» graceSeconds|body|integer \| null|false|The number of grace seconds after expiry of the time when the next ping was expected, before raising an alert. The number of grace seconds to allow before classifying a Measured Monitor task duration as an anomaly.|
|» intervalDays|body|integer \| null|false|The number of days in the expected ping / run / measured / scheduled interval. Can be left blank. Can be specified together with any combination of the other interval fields.|
|» intervalHours|body|integer \| null|false|The number of hours in the expected ping / run / measured / scheduled interval. Can be left blank. Can be specified together with any combination of the other interval fields.|
|» intervalMinutes|body|integer \| null|false|The number of minutes in the expected ping / run / measured / scheduled interval. Can be left blank. Can be specified together with any combination of the other interval fields.|

## Creates a Ping resource.

<a id="opIdapi_ping_post"></a>

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/ping \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "expectNextPingAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "expectNextPingAtEpoch": 0,
    "monitor": "string",
    "pingCustomCode": "string",
    "pingCustomPayload": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/ping`

Creates a Ping resource.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expectNextPingAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "expectNextPingAtEpoch": 0,
  "monitor": "string",
  "pingCustomCode": "string",
  "pingCustomPayload": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="creates-a-ping-resource-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[Ping-post](#schemaping-post)|true|The new Ping resource|
|» expectNextPingAt|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|When to expect the next ping for a Last Ping monitor type. This date-time is always interpreted to be in the timezone of the monitor. Any UTC offset is ignored. Supply either "expectNextPingAt", or "expectNextPingAtEpoch", or a X_NEXT_PING request header, not more than one of those options. Must be blank for other monitor types.|
|» expectNextPingAtEpoch|body|integer \| null|false|When to expect the next ping for a Last Ping monitor type, expressed in epoch timestamp format. Supply either "expectNextPingAt", or "expectNextPingAtEpoch", or a X_NEXT_PING request header, not more than one of those options. Must be blank for other monitor types.|
|» monitor|body|string(iri-reference)|true|The monitor that is related to this resource instance.|
|» pingCustomCode|body|string \| null|false|The client-supplied custom code that is appended to the ping. Only the first 10 characters are used and saved.|
|» pingCustomPayload|body|string \| null|false|The client-supplied custom payload that is saved with the ping. Only the first 100 characters are saved. This value overrides the value of an monitor's alert payload, if the ping results in an alert.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "alertLogs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "createdAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "dataSegmentCode": "string",
  "expectNextPingAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "expectNextPingAtEpoch": 0,
  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "ipAddress": "string",
  "monitor": "string",
  "monitorStatusLog": "string",
  "partition": "string",
  "pingCustomCode": "string",
  "pingCustomPayload": "string",
  "pingMethodCode": "string",
  "resourceOwner": "string"
}
```

|alertService|string(iri-reference)|false|none|The alert service that is related to this resource.|

|partition|string(iri-reference)|false|none|The partition that contains this resource instance. The resource cannot be moved to another partition.|
|ping|string(iri-reference) \| null|false|none|The ping that triggered this resource instance.|
|resourceOwner|string \| null|false|none|The name of the person who owns this resource.|
|webhookResponseBody|string \| null|false|none|The response body returned by a successful request to a webhook URL. Length limited to 1,000 characters.|

The Monitor resource is a collection of services that monitor the presence and/or absence of pings, and follow sets of rules to dispatch or not dispatch alerts.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alertPayloadExtended|string \| null|false|none|Payload that must be sent in the body of each alert when you use your own email or webhook alert services. This is the body for email alerts and the request body for webhook alerts. This text is not sent when using the built-in alert services. Sending user-supplied text via our own email server is too big a risk to our email reputation. Max 2 MB characters.|
|alertPayloadShort|string \| null|false|none|Payload that must be sent in the body of each alert when you use your own short message alert services. This also serves as the subject for email alerts. Not used for webhooks. This text is not sent when using the built-in alert services. Sending user-supplied text via our own email server is too big a risk to our email reputation. Max 100 characters.|
|alertServices|[string(iri-reference)]|false|none|The alert services that are related to this resource.|
|allowUnauthenticatedPings|boolean|false|none|Indicates that the monitor will accept pings that are not OAuth authenticated.|
|contentCheckMustNotExist|boolean|false|none|Indicates that the Web Content monitor must verify the absence of the text or the Xpath node, and dispatch an alert if it is present. The default behavior is to verify the presence of the text or the Xpath node, and dispatch an alert if it is absent.|
|contentCheckText|string \| null|false|none|The text (case-insensitive) that must or must not be present at the contentCheckUrl. If contentCheckXpathFilter is supplied, then the only the text within that nodes is evaluated, otherwise text on the entire web page is evaluated.|
|contentCheckUrl|string(uri) \| null|false|none|The URL that the Web Content monitor type must evaluate for the specified conditions.|
|contentCheckXpathFilter|string \| null|false|none|The Xpath filter (<a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XPath">Xpath</a>, <a href="https://devhints.io/xpath">Xpath Cheatsheet</a>) that selects a specific node in the HTML of the target web page. If contentCheckText is supplied, then only the text within the selected node is evaluated. If contentCheckText is left empty, then the presence or the absence of the selected node is evaluated.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When the resource instance was created. This date-time is in the UTC timezone.|
|dataSegmentCode|string \| null|false|none|User-provided string on which to segment and filter data. Max 50 characters.|
|graceSeconds|integer \| null|false|none|The number of grace seconds after expiry of the time when the next ping was expected, before raising an alert. The number of grace seconds to allow before classifying a Measured Monitor task duration as an anomaly.|
|humanizedInterval|string \| null|false|read-only|The expected ping / run interval of this monitor in human readable form.|
|id|string(uuid) \| null|false|read-only|The unique identifier of the resource instance.|
|internalMonitorName|string|false|none|The internal name of the monitor. This name is used in alerts when you use the built-in alert services. Sending user-supplied text via our own email server is too big a risk to our email reputation. The monitorName field is used when you use your own alert services.|
|intervalDays|integer \| null|false|none|The number of days in the expected ping / run / measured / scheduled interval. Can be left blank. Can be specified together with any combination of the other interval fields.|
|intervalHours|integer \| null|false|none|The number of hours in the expected ping / run / measured / scheduled interval. Can be left blank. Can be specified together with any combination of the other interval fields.|
|intervalMinutes|integer \| null|false|none|The number of minutes in the expected ping / run / measured / scheduled interval. Can be left blank. Can be specified together with any combination of the other interval fields.|
|intervalMonths|integer \| null|false|none|The number of months in the expected ping / run / measured / scheduled interval. Can be left blank. Can be specified together with any combination of the other interval fields.|
|intervalSeconds|integer \| null|false|none|The number of seconds in the expected ping / run / measured / scheduled interval. Can be left blank. Can be specified together with any combination of the other interval fields.|
|intervalYears|integer \| null|false|none|The number of years in the expected ping / run / measured / scheduled interval. Can be left blank. Can be specified together with any combination of the other interval fields.|
|isMonitorPaused|boolean|false|none|Indicates that the monitor is paused and will not send alerts.|
|lastPingAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the last ping was received. This date-time is in the UTC timezone.|
|monitorName|string \| null|true|none|The name of the monitor. Max 255 characters.|
|monitorNotes|string \| null|false|none|Notes about the monitor. Max 10,000 characters. Formatting using Markdown is allowed. HTML will be removed.|
|monitorStatusCode|string(iri-reference)|false|none|The status of the monitor.|
|monitorTypeCode|string(iri-reference) \| null|true|none|The type of the monitor.|
|nextPingAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the next ping is expected. This date-time is in the UTC timezone.|
|partition|string(iri-reference)|true|none|The partition that contains this resource instance. The resource cannot be moved to another partition.|
|pingSecret|string|false|none|A secret key that can be sent in the X_PING_SECRET HTTP request header of a ping for additional security. Sending the secret is recommended for unauthenticated ping requests. It is redundant for OAuth authenticated ping requests that have the "Authorization: Bearer" header.|
|publicDescription|string \| null|false|none|A text description of the monitor that is accessible to unauthenticated users that receive an alert from the monitor. Formatting using Markdown is allowed. HTML will be removed.|
|resourceOwner|string \| null|false|none|The name of the person who owns this resource.|
|startMonitorAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When to start the Regular Interval type monitor or Heartbeat type monitor, or when to send the first alert of the Scheduled Repeatable Alert monitor. Cannot be blank for a Regular Interval, Heartbeat, or Scheduled Repeatable Alert type monitor, must be blank for other monitors types. This date-time is always interpreted to be in the timezone of the monitor. Any UTC offset is ignored.|
|startMonitorAtUtc|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|The startMonitorAt date-time in the UTC timezone.|
|systemMessages|[string]|false|none|Service notes regarding the resource.|
|timezoneCode|string(iri-reference)|true|none|The timezone of the monitor. Dates and times in alerts and reports will be in this time zone.|
|webResponseSecondsLimit|integer \| null|false|none|The time in seconds that the Web Response monitor type must allow for the web page to respond.|
|webResponseUrl|string(uri) \| null|false|none|The URL that the Web Response monitor type must evaluate for the specified conditions.|

The Ping resource is a collection of pings that have been sent to monitors in the user account.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alertLogs|[string(iri-reference)]|false|none|The alert logs that are related to this resource instance.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When the resource instance was created. This date-time is in the UTC timezone.|
|dataSegmentCode|string \| null|false|none|User-provided string on which to segment and filter data. Max 50 characters.|
|expectNextPingAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When to expect the next ping for a Last Ping monitor type. This date-time is always interpreted to be in the timezone of the monitor. Any UTC offset is ignored. Supply either "expectNextPingAt", or "expectNextPingAtEpoch", or a X_NEXT_PING request header, not more than one of those options. Must be blank for other monitor types.|
|expectNextPingAtEpoch|integer \| null|false|none|When to expect the next ping for a Last Ping monitor type, expressed in epoch timestamp format. Supply either "expectNextPingAt", or "expectNextPingAtEpoch", or a X_NEXT_PING request header, not more than one of those options. Must be blank for other monitor types.|
|id|string(uuid) \| null|false|read-only|The unique identifier of the resource instance.|
|ipAddress|string \| null|false|none|The IP address where this resource originated.|
|monitor|string(iri-reference)|true|none|The monitor that is related to this resource instance.|
|monitorStatusLog|string(iri-reference) \| null|false|none|The monitor status that resulted from the ping.|
|partition|string(iri-reference)|false|none|The partition that contains this resource instance. The resource cannot be moved to another partition.|
|pingCustomCode|string \| null|false|none|The client-supplied custom code that is appended to the ping. Only the first 10 characters are used and saved.|
|pingCustomPayload|string \| null|false|none|The client-supplied custom payload that is saved with the ping. Only the first 100 characters are saved. This value overrides the value of an monitor's alert payload, if the ping results in an alert.|
|pingMethodCode|string(iri-reference)|false|none|The method of the ping.|
|resourceOwner|string \| null|false|none|The name of the person who owns this resource.|

```json
{
  "dataSegmentCode": "string",
  "partition": "string",
  "transportName": "string",
  "zendeskEmail": "user@example.com",
  "zendeskHost": "example.com",
  "zendeskToken": "string"
}
```

The TransportZendesk resource is a collection of transports that carry dispatched alerts to the external Zendesk service.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dataSegmentCode|string \| null|false|none|User-provided string on which to segment and filter data. Max 50 characters.|
|partition|string(iri-reference)|true|none|The partition that contains this resource instance. The resource cannot be moved to another partition.|
|transportName|string \| null|true|none|The name of the transport.|
|zendeskEmail|string(email) \| null|true|none|The login email address for the Zendesk service.|
|zendeskHost|string(hostname) \| null|true|none|The host name for the Zendesk service (domain.zendesk.com).|
|zendeskToken|string \| null|true|none|The token for the Zendesk service. Stored in encrypted format.|

The UserAccount resource contains basic information regarding the authenticated user account.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accountLevelCode|string(iri-reference)|false|none|The account level of the user.|
|creditsOveragePercentTripSwitch|integer \| null|false|none|If the credits consumed in the billing period are this percentage above the account plan's included credits, cease further consumption of credits until the end of the billing period. Any integer between 1 and 1,000. Optional. Leave blank for no limit.|
|email|string \| null|false|none|The email address of the user.|
|firstName|string|false|none|The first name of the user.|
|id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|The unique identifier of the resource instance.|
|isDelinquent|boolean|false|none|Whether the user account has overdue payments.|
|lastName|string \| null|false|none|The last name of the user.|
|timezoneCode|string(iri-reference)|false|none|The timezone of the user.|
